phrases: Spring's JUnit support loads our configuration before the test. It creates a repository and supplies it to our service.
Ask the context for the service. This confirms the required bean can actually be retrieved.
Compare its repository with the context's repository. Assert they're the same object. Matching values aren't enough.
Run the smoke test. It passes: context loaded, required bean found, expected dependency confirmed.
This smoke test covers our selected configuration and wiring. Order behavior needs separate tests. Load, look up, assert.
hook_original: Your app starts, but did Spring wire it?
hook_refinement_reason: Shortens the spoken hook to land within two seconds and asks whether expected wiring was checked without implying successful context startup establishes comprehensive correctness.
semantic_scope: SpringJUnitConfig selected Config loads; getBean required OrderService and Repo; assertSame(service.repository(),contextRepo). A passing smoke test does not prove order behavior or other configurations; no full application test claim.
